content: This medication is indicated for the treatment of human smallpox disease caused by the variola virus in both adult and pediatric patients, including neonates. For patients weighing 48 kg or more, the recommended dosage is 200 mg orally once weekly for two doses (on Days 1 and 8). For patients weighing less than 48 kg, the dosage is 4 mg/kg orally once weekly for two doses (on Days 1 and 8). For patients weighing less than 10 kg, the dosage is 6 mg/kg orally once weekly for two doses (on Days 1 and 8). Currently, there is no available data on the efficacy of this medication in treating monkeypox in humans. However, it has demonstrated effectiveness against orthopoxviruses in laboratory (in vitro) and animal studies. As of June 17, 2022, the CDC is working on developing an emergency access investigational new drug to facilitate its use as a treatment. This medication is not currently available through the United States Strategic National Stockpile. Coadministration of enasidenib with this medication may increase its levels or effects, potentially leading to serious toxicities. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, administer this medication at least three hours before enasidenib. Additionally, enasidenib should not be coadministered with sensitive OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates, as even minimal concentration changes may result in significant toxicities. Ublituximab may reduce the effects of this medication due to its immunosuppressive properties, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely in such cases. In clinical trials, an increased incidence of mortality was observed in individuals treated with this medication compared to those receiving a placebo when evaluated for another disease over a 24-week period. Based on findings from animal reproduction studies, this medication may cause fetal harm if administered to pregnant individuals. Pregnancy testing should be performed in individuals of childbearing potential before initiating treatment. This medication is excreted as metabolites, with 51% eliminated in urine and 40% in feces. It is suspected to be a carcinogen, and direct contact with broken or crushed tablets or oral suspension should be avoided. If contact with skin or mucous membranes occurs, wash thoroughly with soap and water, and rinse eyes thoroughly with water. Store the medication at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with permissible excursions between 15–30°C (59–86°F). Do not freeze. The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only. Formulary information may vary, and it is recommended to contact the applicable plan provider for the most current details.
